items.title: Army to detonate lead azide explosives in Iowa
items.feedTitle: Army plans to detonate Iowa stockpile on Wednesday, tells public there's no reason to panic
items.summary: The U.S. Army is set to detonate approximately five tons of lead azide bomb-making material at an Iowa ammunition facility on Wednesday, after rescheduling the operation multiple times due to public health concerns. The detonation has drawn significant controversy over potential toxic lead exposure, with residents warned to stay indoors with windows closed. A federal appeals court cleared the way for the controlled destruction, which officials say is the safest course of action for the unstable explosives.

items.title: Consumer confidence surges in November after midterm wins
items.feedTitle: Consumer sentiment surged in November: Conference Board
items.summary: The Conference Board reported consumer confidence spiked to 103.3 in November from 91.9 in October, a 11.4-point jump that exceeded economists' expectations. The surge follows Democrats' sweeping midterm victories and reflects improved sentiment as the year closes.

items.title: Severe Thanksgiving storms threaten millions nationwide
items.feedTitle: Severe Thanksgiving storms threaten millions of travelers nationwide and Macy’s Day parade
items.summary: Powerful storms are threatening millions of Thanksgiving travelers on both U.S. coasts, with risk of significant disruptions to air travel, road conditions, and outdoor events including the Macy's Day Parade. Airlines continue to recover from recent tech failures, adding to operational challenges during the busy holiday period.

items.title: Trump personally intervened to reinstate Jensen Huang
items.feedTitle: Why Trump pushed for Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
items.summary: President Trump personally pushed for Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO just two weeks after he resigned amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence. Trump publicly stated he believed Huang did nothing wrong, overriding concerns from lawmakers and national security officials.

items.title: DOJ recovers $8B in largest anti-scam crackdown
items.feedTitle: DOJ recovers $8B, charges more than 800 suspects in largest anti-scam surge in history
items.summary: The Department of Justice announced the largest anti-scam surge in U.S. history, recovering $8 billion and charging more than 800 suspects across various fraud schemes. The operation targets widespread consumer fraud affecting Americans nationwide.

stlouis.title: Former St. Louis prosecutor Kim Gardner disbarred
stlouis.feedTitle: Former St. Louis City Circuit Attorney Kim Gardner disbarred
stlouis.summary: The Missouri Supreme Court has disbarred former St. Louis City Circuit Attorney Kim Gardner, the high-profile prosecutor whose tenure was marked by significant cases and controversial decisions. This represents a major professional consequence for Gardner's leadership of the office.

stlouis.title: St. Louis area faces winter storm watch
stlouis.feedTitle: Metro-east, St. Louis under a winter storm watch for possible ‘heavy’ snow - Belleville News-Democrat
stlouis.summary: The St. Louis metro and Metro-east region are under a winter storm watch for the coming days, with forecasts calling for possible heavy snow during Thanksgiving travel. The weather is expected to transition from rain to snow Wednesday night, potentially impacting holiday plans.

stlouis.title: Webster Groves senior housing project clears funding
stlouis.feedTitle: Webster Groves senior housing project secures key funding as $12 million plan clears major hurdle
stlouis.summary: A $12 million senior housing development in Webster Groves has secured key funding and cleared a major hurdle in the approval process, moving the project closer to construction.

items.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets
items.feedTitle: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
items.summary: Huawei was convicted of stealing trade secrets in a New York federal trial but acquitted of racketeering charges. The verdict follows a months-long trial and addresses allegations of intellectual property theft.

items.title: Cuba's life expectancy falls for first time since 1950
items.feedTitle: Life expectancy in Cuba falls for first time since 1950 amid economic crisis
items.summary: Life expectancy in Cuba has fallen to 74.4 years in 2025 from 78.8 in 2020, the first decline since 1950, amid a severe economic crisis. The World Health Organization has highlighted the concerning trend as the island grapples with economic hardship.

items.title: Armed men seize 25 hostages at Colombian supermarket
items.feedTitle: Armed men take 25 hostages at supermarket in one of Colombia’s top tourist destinations
items.summary: A group of armed men with covered faces seized a supermarket in Cartagena, Colombia, one of the country's top tourist destinations, taking 25 people hostage. Police reportedly deployed snipers to surrounding buildings as the incident unfolded.

items.title: Bangladesh's ousted leader plans December 16 return
items.feedTitle: Bangladesh’s ousted leader Hasina plans to return home from exile on Dec 16
items.summary: Sheikh Hasina, Bangladesh's ousted leader in exile, has announced plans to return to her home country on December 16. The stated return date marks a significant political development in the nation's ongoing turmoil.

items.title: Businesses supporting Ukraine warned of Russian sabotage
items.feedTitle: Businesses supporting Ukraine told to 'act now' to protect against Russian sabotage
items.summary: British officials and MI5 have warned UK companies supplying Ukraine's military to prepare for Russian sabotage threats. The advisory reflects growing concerns about Moscow's efforts to disrupt Western support for Kyiv across new regions of conflict.

items.title: India's space economy to reach $40-45 billion by 2036
items.feedTitle: India’s space economy projected to rise to $40-45 billion by 2036: Minister Jitendra Singh
items.summary: India's Space Minister Jitendra Singh projects the nation's space economy will grow to $40–45 billion within the next decade, driven significantly by private sector expansion. The forecast reflects India's growing ambitions in satellite launches, manufacturing, and commercial space ventures.

items.title: India deepens authoritarian slide under Modi, report finds
items.feedTitle: India news: Nation deepens authoritarian slide under Modi — report
items.summary: A report assesses that India has undergone further democratic backsliding under Prime Minister Modi's governance. The analysis points to weakening institutional checks and rising authoritarian practices in the nation's political system.

items.title: CJP's Saurav Das stopped at Delhi airport over error
items.feedTitle: Indian government has 'lost the plot', says 'cockroach' leader barred from UK flight
items.summary: Saurav Das, chief justice of a prominent organization, was barred from boarding a UK flight at Delhi airport after his passport was flagged, allegedly due to a birthplace error. He criticized the Indian government, saying it has 'lost the plot,' drawing attention to administrative failures.

items.title: US weighs fresh tariffs on India and 14 other nations
items.feedTitle: US weighs fresh tariffs on India, China and 14 other trading partners
items.summary: The Trump administration is planning to impose new tariff increases on India, China, and 14 other trading partners as part of a broader trade policy review. The proposed action reflects the administration's protectionist stance on excess factory capacity.

items.title: India pledges $1.6B flood relief for Nepal
items.feedTitle: India pledges $1.6bn in flood relief for Nepal as Balendra Shah visits Modi
items.summary: India has announced a $1.6 billion commitment in flood relief aid for Nepal following recent disasters. The pledge reflects India's neighboring country support and comes amid discussions on deepening bilateral defense and information security ties.

immigration.title: DOL proposes sweeping PERM labor certification changes
immigration.feedTitle: Modernizing the Labor Market Test and Improving Protections for U.S. Workers in the PERM Immigrant Visa Program
immigration.summary: The U.S. Department of Labor has proposed major reforms to the PERM (Permanent Labor Certification) program, including a 90-day recruitment requirement and a two-year bar on PERM filings by employers with recent layoffs in the same job category. The proposed rule, not yet finalized, would significantly tighten employment-based green card sponsorship standards and affect hundreds of thousands of pending cases. The changes are designed to strengthen protections for U.S. workers and modernize labor market testing.

immigration.title: DHS proposes ending deference to prior H-1B approvals
immigration.feedTitle: DHS Proposes to End Deference to Prior Approvals on H-1B and Other I-129 Extensions
immigration.summary: The Department of Homeland Security has proposed ending the practice of deferring to prior approvals when adjudicating H-1B visa extension petitions. This proposed change, not yet finalized, could affect renewals and work-visa continuity for thousands of workers, potentially making it harder to maintain status.

immigration.title: US proposes ending green card fast-track for nurses
immigration.feedTitle: US proposes ending green card fast track for foreign nurses and physical therapists
immigration.summary: The U.S. government has proposed eliminating the expedited green card pathway for foreign nurses and physical therapists under the Schedule A category. This proposed rule would remove long-standing priority processing for these healthcare professions, affecting recruitment in critical shortage areas.

items.title: Tech stocks slide as Nvidia euphoria fades
items.feedTitle: Tech sell-off resumes as euphoria from Jensen Huang’s Nvidia return subsides
items.summary: Technology shares led a broad market retreat Tuesday as caution returned after Jensen Huang's extraordinary return to Nvidia. Nvidia shares fell 7–9% as investors, still euphoric over their AI-driven rally, faced questions about the sustainability of AI sector valuations amid broader economic uncertainties.

items.title: Anthropic shares tumble below $83 IPO price
items.feedTitle: Anthropic shares tumble below $83 IPO price, on track to lose nearly $200 billion in value
items.summary: Anthropic's stock has fallen below its $83 IPO price on its fourth trading day, tracking toward losses of nearly $200 billion in market value. The decline signals investor concerns about sky-high AI startup valuations and the company's business model sustainability, despite largely positive analyst sentiment.

items.title: Consumer confidence shoots up after midterm victories
items.feedTitle: Consumer confidence shoots up after Democrats' midterm victories — though inflation worries persist
items.summary: U.S. consumer confidence surged in November as voters and investors digest Democrats' sweeping midterm victories and retreating gas prices, though inflation worries persist. The Conference Board's index jumped 11.4 points, marking a sharp reversal in sentiment.

items.title: Oil tanker hits in Strait of Hormuz amid Iran tensions
items.feedTitle: Global Markets: Oil tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz - Manitoba Co-operator
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps reported that three oil tankers escorted through the Strait of Hormuz were struck by underwater mines, raising concerns about global energy supplies and regional stability. The incident underscores ongoing Middle East tensions.

cards.title: Attention fragmentation costs compound
cards.insight: Each context switch to email, chat, or notifications carries a cognitive recovery cost—research shows it takes 23 minutes to regain full focus. The cumulative loss of focus time is invisible but adds up to weeks of lost productivity per year.
cards.takeaway: Block time for deep work without notifications; batch communications into 2–3 windows daily rather than continuous checking.

cards.title: Energy management beats time management
cards.insight: Willpower and mental clarity follow circadian and ultradian rhythms; your peak focus window is typically 90–120 minutes, not 8 hours. Pushing past fatigue yields diminishing returns and cascading errors.
cards.takeaway: Schedule high-stakes or creative work during your proven peak hours; protect that window more jealously than any meeting.

cards.title: Clarity precedes speed
cards.insight: Vague goals or unclear next steps create decision paralysis and task-switching. A five-minute planning session that eliminates ambiguity compounds focus and momentum throughout the day.
cards.takeaway: Before starting a session, write down the specific output you're aiming for—not 'work on report,' but 'finish chart 3 and get review feedback.'

cards.title: Environment shapes willpower more than discipline
cards.insight: Willpower is finite; relying on discipline to resist distractions is costly. Removing friction for good habits and adding friction to bad ones (e.g., phone in another room) is more effective than self-control.
cards.takeaway: Redesign your work environment: silence notifications, close unnecessary tabs, position tools you need and hide ones you don't.

ai.title: Anthropic shares fall below IPO price amid broader sell-off
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic shares fall below IPO price, a worrying sign for AI startups

ai.title: OpenAI, Anthropic staff fear unreleased AI model safety
ai.feedTitle: OpenAI, Anthropic Staff Fear New Model Releases: Axios
ai.summary: More than two dozen AI researchers from OpenAI and Anthropic have expressed alarm that unreleased models from their companies may pose too significant safety risks to deploy. The internal concerns highlight ongoing tensions between advancing capabilities and responsible deployment timelines.

ai.title: Harvard, Nvidia secure $12M DOE quantum AI error correction award
ai.feedTitle: Harvard, QuEra, NVIDIA, Anthropic, and Three National Labs Secure $12 Million DOE Award for AI-Driven Quantum Error Correction
ai.summary: A consortium including Harvard University, QuEra, Nvidia, Anthropic, and three national laboratories has received a $12 million Department of Energy grant to develop AI-driven quantum error correction technologies. The award signals growing federal investment in AI-quantum integration.

ai.title: Avicena raises $100M for microLED AI chip interconnect
ai.feedTitle: Avicena raises $100M to link AI chips with microLEDs instead of lasers
ai.summary: Avicena has raised $100 million in funding to develop microLED-based interconnect technology for AI chips, offering an alternative to laser-based systems. The advance targets improving efficiency and performance in AI hardware design.

ai.title: FCA publishes vision for agentic AI regulation
ai.feedTitle: FCA Publishes Future Vision of Agentic AI Regulation -
ai.summary: The UK Financial Conduct Authority has published its regulatory framework for agentic AI systems, defining how autonomous AI agents should be supervised in the financial sector. The guidance reflects growing regulatory attention to increasingly autonomous AI deployments.
